output.name: Sekul
output.myth: In the year of the great thaw, Tavo the Gale laughed and the valleys ran full. Brown water came off the hills and sank the lower boats at their moorings, and the children stood in the shallows with nothing but their hands. Aun was on the cliff mending a kite, and he was ashamed that his knife had let so much loose sky. He took the gourd from his own boat, scraped it clean and bored a handle through its neck. Then he went down into the flood and bailed for three days without sleep. Skeru the Asking Raven, who had lost her questions to Tavo, sat on the north-east stake and watched him work. When he was done his palms were raw and every boat was floating. Hesk the Reel counted them and found none lost. She wound the gourd on a string and hung it in Vel, where the thaw could see it, near the Knot Belt where Aun tied his days of labour. Now when the floods come down, Sekul rises over the Lamp Road, and the people go to the water with their own gourds.
output.finding: Find the Knot Belt on the Lamp Road, then look a fist and a little more (about 13°) south-east of it for Sekul.
